Inter-domain mobility in human multi-domain proteins

A template-based centroid screen across the reviewed human kinome and the complete eligible non-kinase proteome, plus a ΔΔG feasibility study. Figures embedded · generated 28 October 2026 · chervov/ProteinModelling1

1  Where this started: AlphaFold PAE 2  The JAK anchor 3  The reviewed human kinome 4  Non-kinase proteins, to exhaustion 5  What the motions look like 6  ΔΔG at scale 7  Caveats
Method in one sentence. For every protein, take all SWISS-MODEL templates and the AlphaFold model, define domains from UniProt Domain features, compute the Cα centroid of each domain, and compare all pairwise inter-centroid distances across templates. Distances are rotation-invariant, so no superposition is needed; a wide spread across independent templates means the two domains move relative to one another.

1  Where this started: AlphaFold PAE

The predicted aligned error matrix shows which parts of a chain have a fixed relative orientation. Blocks on the diagonal are rigid modules; dark off-diagonal blocks mean two modules are not positioned relative to each other.

The screen is one-directional. A multi-module call is strong evidence of a joint. A single-module call says almost nothing — SRC-family and SYK/ZAP70 came out as single bodies only because AlphaFold predicts their closed autoinhibited state. One PAE cluster means model certainty, not rigidity.

2  The JAK anchor

The JAK family was used to test whether the method recovers a motion that is already known. It does, and it localises the hinge.

Direct measurement on the cryo-EM dimers confirms it: 7T6F and 8EWY give an identical FERM–SH2–JH2 block (38.8 / 47.7 / 39.9 Å) while JH1 moves — FERM–JH1 84.1 Å versus 94.1 Å.

3  The reviewed human kinome

All 480 reviewed human kinases (InterPro IPR000719). 233 have two or more UniProt domain features; 2,435 gated observations yielded 270 comparable pairs across 86 proteins.

quantityvalue
pairs with ≥2 distinct parent templates270
spread > 15 Å64
spread > 20 Å46
AlphaFold outside the experimental range75 / 269 (28%)
A result that should give pause. AKT1–3 PH↔kinase is invariant across 11 parent templates (24.0–26.3 Å) — yet AlphaFold places it at 33–35 Å, outside the entire experimental range.

4  Non-kinase proteins, to exhaustion

The non-kinase screen is complete. All 3,397 reviewed human non-kinase proteins with two or more domain features (200–3,000 aa) were screened; exactly 354 have the two or more distinct multi-domain templates needed to measure anything, and all 354 were analysed across three batches. The remaining 3,043 are not excluded by choice — no inter-template comparison exists for them.

The sharpest AlphaFold failure found. α-actinin-2 and -4 are genuine rods — a single chain of 859 modelled residues spanning 280 Å, verified directly in the coordinates. AlphaFold places the same domain pairs at 56–70 Å, an error of roughly 200 Å, while modelling the domains themselves correctly (EF-hand-1↔EF-hand-2 is 11.9 Å in templates and AlphaFold alike). Only the long-range arrangement collapses.

5  What the motions look like

Two template lineages per protein, superposed on the first domain of the pair and projected onto their shared principal plane. Cα trace coloured by UniProt domain in sequence order; the dashed line joins the two centroids being measured.

6  ΔΔG at scale

Separate study: how to compute stability changes for large numbers of human variants. Download before computing — EBI's ProtVar already publishes FoldX ΔΔG for 208,792,558 human missense variants, covering 76.0% of canonical human residues.

Measured throughput on this machine, 8 CPU cores and no GPU: 280 variants/s sustained. Full saturation of JAK1 (1,154 aa, 21,926 variants) takes 65 s; the uncovered quarter of the proteome is 6.4 hours on 8 cores. ProtVar coverage is worst in the 1,001–2,700 aa band (64.1%) — exactly the multi-domain range screened above.

7  Caveats that bound every number here

issueconsequence
Centroid distance is blind to distance-preserving rotationsAn entire class of motion is invisible — demonstrated by SHP2 at 2.1 Å over 20 parents
PDB-provider files use author numberingRejected by the 80% residue-identity gate — 223 of 359 files in batch 3, all PDB-provider. Fix is PDBe SIFTS mapping
Templates are shared between paraloguesIdentical values are one observation seen twice, not two — check entry overlap before calling a replicate
UniProt Domain features onlyRTK ectodomain subdomains are missed, so EGFR, ERBB2, ERBB4 and LTK drop out silently
SWISS-MODEL models are declustered, PDB-relayed entries are notPooling them as equal parent counts overweights the latter
Pairs resting on 2 entriesProvisional, not established — IGF2R, TMPRSS15, IGHG4, ACTN2/4
